relevance_note: Case report of a neonate with HA20 caused by a deletion including TNFAIP3, plus a table of 11 previously reported 6q-deletion patients: 'revealed a heterozygous 5.15 Mb deletion in 6q23.3q24.3'.
method_note: Read the whole paper; built the JSON with a Python script in my scratch directory that transcribed Table 1 (patients as columns) and generated the row spans; I checked the transcription cell by cell against the table, and every span was then checked verbatim against the paper. Table 1 column headers: second header row 'Patient 1'...'Patient 12'; first header row gives the source ('Current report', then author names). Empty first-row cells after 'Endo et al.', 'Tsuchida et al.' and 'Wu et al.' were read as merged header cells, so Patients 2-3 = Endo et al., 7-8 = Tsuchida et al., 11-12 = Wu et al. (inferred from layout). The reference-list entry for each author name is added as a second span. Patient 1 ('Current report') is the neonate described first-hand in the text; Patients 2-12 are previously published cases from Table 1. Per rule 6, '-' cells were treated as not reported, even though the table uses 'Not mentioned' separately and '-' may mean absent; so no Table 1 '-' produced an excluded row. Table 1 lists only initial features. Per rule 8, Table 1 'de novo' (Patients 1, 4, 5, 6, 11) was not recorded as de novo inheritance because no parental testing is described; the statement is kept in parental_testing_statement. Checklist 'recurrent fever' was set observed for patients with Fever '+' because the seven '+' patients are exactly those whose initial symptoms include fever, and the text says 'in seven patients, the initial symptoms were unprovoked and recurrent episodes of fever'. 'Respiratory- infections' (Patient 4) and 'Infections' (Patient 11) were recorded as features, but the checklist 'recurrent infections' was left not reported (recurrence not stated). Gastroenteritis was mapped to GI inflammation; Henoch-Schönlein purpura to vasculitis and skin lesions; rosacea to skin lesions. Patient 1 uveitis/ocular inflammation was set excluded from 'No other obvious abnormalities were found in ophthalmologic assessment'. AIHA is excluded for Patient 1 but autoimmune cytopenia is left not reported (narrower absence). Phenotypes in reference titles were not used. NBSP characters in the table were normalised to spaces in values only; spans are exact. n_patients_reported = 12 counts the 11 literature patients plus the one new patient. Contradictions or inconsistencies in the paper: (1) deletion band '6q23.3q24.3' in the text vs '6q23.2q24.3' in the Fig. 1 legend; (2) fever 'resolved gradually within 24 days' vs WBC/CRP normalised 'accompanied by extinguished fever within 22 days'; (3) the text says 'Nine patients experienced early-onset symptoms before the age of 1 year old', but Table 1 shows seven with onset under 1 year (nine if '1 year' is counted); (4) TORCH serology including Cytomegalovirus reported 'normal' while mNGS/PCR detected CMV, so both rows are recorded; (5) abdominal ultrasonography 'no other abnormalitis except for hepatomegaly' sits alongside splenomegaly on physical examination; no excluded splenomegaly row was emitted because the spleen is not named. Age at last evaluation (six months) is the latest dated evaluation in the text; follow-up was then suspended.
